howToTest: In the probe bio: `<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" width="320" height="180" title="t" allow="autoplay" loading="lazy" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>`. curl and check whether it is stored as a live <iframe>, as a button.embed_preload with data-embed_code, or escaped, and which attributes remain.
whyItMatters: 0 iframes in 50 sampled bios. allow/loading are shown dropped only on a jam page; title has never been seen on any stored iframe, so whether embeds can have an accessible name is still open.

question: Are the 6 never-seen properties of the 27-list (padding-top, background-image, border-width, border-color, border-style, min-width) kept, and are border-radius and display really dropped from inline style?
howToTest: In the probe bio: `uvw`. curl and compare. The library predicts all 7 kept and the last two become style="".
whyItMatters: The 27-property list is a library model. 21 properties are confirmed live, and only one live negative is known (border-radius on a Spotify iframe).

question: Does itch's profile cap count characters, UTF-8 bytes or UTF-16 units, and what happens past it: refused save or truncation? This decides whether the budget sentence can drop its byte clause.
howToTest: On a CSS-enabled test profile, save each sheet below, then read `<style id="custom_css">` back logged out with curl (raw copy to the scratchpad), noting whether the save failed or what was stored. (a) Exactly 5,120 ASCII characters. (b) 5,121 ASCII characters: is it refused or truncated? (c) 5,110 characters including 10 × `→`, which is 5,130 bytes: accepted means the cap counts characters, refused means bytes. (d) 5,115 characters including 10 × 😀, which is 5,125 UTF-16 units and 5,145 bytes: separates code points from UTF-16 units. Use one-line CSS made of padding comments plus one rule, and run the 01 §3 snippet on each file before saving.
whyItMatters: The canonical budget sentence keeps both chars and bytes ≤ 5,120 only because the unit is unknown. Knowing the unit and the over-cap behaviour would let the KB give one exact number.

question: Do the minifier outputs render identically in Firefox and Safari? Only Chromium was compared.
howToTest: Install a Firefox build (e.g. `npx playwright install firefox`, after the user approves the download) or open the pages in desktop Firefox and Safari. Rebuild the harness pages with `python -I build-harness.py fixture <S>/out` and `build-fb-harness.py`, serve them on 127.0.0.1, then read the same computed values as `probe.mjs` / `probe-fb.mjs` (e.g. with Playwright's `page.evaluate`). Diff each output against its `.source` page. Firefox 158 should keep `content:"*" / ""` working and lose `width:stretch` (it supports only `-webkit-fill-available`, from 146).
whyItMatters: Several fallbacks dropped by lightningcss and csso matter only in non-Chromium engines. The static diffs show what those engines would receive, but their real rendering is unverified.

question: Is cssnano (default preset) safe for itch CSS? Does it keep fallback pairs, nesting, range media, `@layer` before `@import`, and `content` strings?
howToTest: In a scratch dir, after the user approves the npm download, run `npm i cssnano postcss postcss-cli`. Then run `npx postcss fixture/src.css --use cssnano -o out/main.cssnano.css`, and the same for `src-layerfirst.css`, `fallbacks.css` and `modern.css`. Then run `build-harness.py`, `build-fb-harness.py`, `probe.mjs`, `probe-fb.mjs` and `fb-table.py` from knowledge/evidence/gapfill09-tools, and add a row to the 09 #44 table.
whyItMatters: cssnano is one of the most common minifiers. The 09 #44 table marks it 'untested, diff before use'.

question: Do the CLI binaries (lightningcss-cli, csso-cli, esbuild CLI) behave exactly like the Node APIs that were tested? Does `esbuild --target=…` (nesting lowering) or `--bundle` (`@import` inlining) change the verdict?
howToTest: With the user's approval for the download, install lightningcss-cli and csso-cli. Run `lightningcss --minify [--targets '>= 0.25%'] fixture/src.css`, `csso fixture/src.css [--no-restructure]` and `esbuild fixture/src.css --minify [--charset=utf8] [--target=chrome100,safari15] [--bundle]`. Byte-compare the results with knowledge/evidence/gapfill09-tools/outputs/main.*.css, then rerun the probes for any variant that differs.
whyItMatters: 09 #44 recommends `esbuild --minify --charset=utf8` by its CLI name. The flag-to-API mapping is tagged [inferred].

question: Sections 01, 02 and 07 still state the budget differently: 01 says '≤ 5,120 characters, with a margin', 02 says 'about 5 KB' and 07 says 'about 5,120 characters'. 01 §3 also lacks the safe-minifier table and still lists only a regex-minifier pitfall. Those files were outside this pass.
howToTest: In 01 (TL;DR item 3 and §3 'What to do'), 02 (size table and checklist item 6) and 07 §7.1 item 6, insert verbatim: 'Budget: ≤ 5,120 characters and ≤ 5,120 UTF-8 bytes, keeping at least 30 spare.' Copy or link the 09 #44 safe-minifier table into 01 §3, citing gapfill09-03 to gapfill09-18. Then grep all sections for '5,000', 'about 5 KB' and 'about 5,120' to confirm one wording remains.
whyItMatters: The gap asked for one budget sentence used word for word across the KB. Until 01, 02 and 07 match, an AI reader still sees three formulations.

question: What does a logged-in NON-owner visitor receive on a profile, a project page, a devlog post and /comments? Specifically: does #user_tools stay, does a site header (.has_header / .has_site_header) appear, does .game_cell_tools appear on profile cards, does the comment form render inside .game_comments_widget with the classes in §11, and does body.dark_theme apply for a dark-mode account?
howToTest: The user logs in with any account and saves another creator's profile, one of that creator's project pages, a devlog post and /comments via 'Save page as… → Webpage, HTML only', once in light site theme and once in dark. Redact csrf_token values, then run knowledge/evidence/section03-tools/skel.py <file> 9 and matrix2.py against the logged-out captures. Also grep for game_cell_tools, post_form, markdown_toolbar, dark_theme, has_header, has_site_header and user_tools.
whyItMatters: Broad rules such as #wrapper textarea/button/li, card overlays and z-index layers in the top-right corner may break UI that only logged-in visitors see. Body-level headers change the top spacing.

question: What is the owner's view of a project page and a devlog post? Is #wrapper inside .game_page_apperance_columns > .game_page_primary_column, is div.game_header_widget (.publish_status, .edit_theme_btn) before it, and does the editor hide #user_tools, .above_game_banner and .goal_banner_widget?
howToTest: The project owner saves their own project page and one devlog post while logged in ('HTML only'), both with the theme editor closed and open. Then run skel.py <file> 9 and head.py, and check the ancestors of #wrapper and the body children.
whyItMatters: This shows whether body > #wrapper selectors fail in the editor, and whether the owner's preview differs from what visitors see (missing strips, scroll container).

question: Does a current (October 2026) owner export of a profile still pre-render hidden items inside #wrapper: inline style="display: none" on hidden projects and collection rows, and section.purchased_games without .mode_show_purchases? Does this shift :nth-child() counts relative to the public page?
howToTest: The profile owner saves their profile logged in ('HTML only') with at least one hidden project or collection and 'Supported by' turned off. Count inline display:none occurrences and .game_cell/.collection_row siblings, and diff them against a logged-out capture taken the same minute (fetch.sh).
whyItMatters: The new §5.4 rules (never force display with !important on those items, never key layout on :nth-child of cards) rest on a single June 2026 export.

question: Is the 'big video' layout (.header_buy_row → .video_embed.big_video → .columns, with no .video_embed left in .right_col) stable across projects? Only one project has been seen so far.
howToTest: Within the request budget, sample more pages from itch.io/games/css and itch.io/games/on-sale listings (≥7 s spacing) and grep for 'big_video'. Run kinds.py and skel.py on every hit. Alternatively, a creator enables the big-video option on a test project and saves the logged-out page.
whyItMatters: Rules such as '.right_col .video_embed' break on that layout; with n=1 its tree is provisional.

question: Do 01 §3 and 09 #41 now quote the canonical size figures from gapfill03-01? I did not edit them because they are out of this task's scope.
howToTest: Whoever owns those sections should replace '93,105 chars' with '93,105 chars CRLF-normalised (93,948 B served; 69,436 chars of data: URIs)' and give the jam as '20,410 host chars (20,411 with itch's trailing space)', citing gapfill03-01. Then grep the three sections for 38,576, 93,105, 20,203 and 20,410 to confirm the wording is consistent.
whyItMatters: An AI reading 01 or 09 alone could still quote a ceiling without its metric or sample.

question: Gap 3: do the Firefox and Safari/WebKit cells of the support matrix and the cross-browser warnings hold when actually run? The warnings cover: an @import dropped because a selector is invalid in another engine, & inside @scope, backdrop-filter with var(), alt text for generated content, the colour of outline:auto, @starting-style on first render, view transitions, MIME strictness, cookie partitioning, and finite-motion behaviour.
howToTest: 1. With the user's explicit go-ahead, run `npx playwright install firefox webkit`. It downloads roughly 100–200 MB of browser binaries; the Playwright cache on this machine holds only chromium-1217, and no Firefox is installed. 2. In firefox.launch() and webkit.launch(), load: knowledge/evidence/support-probe.html; sec07-tools/sec07-probe.html, sec07-probe2.html and sec07-target.html; support-tools/verify2/v2-probe.html; knowledge/tests/index.html (via the :8090 and :8091 servers); the section08-tools framework lab; and gapfill07-tools/finite-motion.html. 3. Record the results per engine and retag the FF/Sa halves in §7.4 as 'verified (Playwright WebKit ≠ Safari)'.
whyItMatters: Safari and iOS Safari are about 18 % of users. Every Firefox/Safari support claim and every cross-browser warning in 07 is documented only, so an AI cannot know whether a fallback is needed in practice.

question: iOS-only behaviour: does the theme-editor background with background-attachment:fixed scroll with the page on iOS Safari, and do dvh units track the toolbar there?
howToTest: Open a test profile on a real iPhone (or a BrowserStack iOS Safari session), scroll, and compare the panel image with a position:fixed pseudo-element layer. Then measure an element sized 100dvh before and after the toolbar collapses.
whyItMatters: §7.13 recommends a fixed pseudo-element layer as the portable backdrop, based only on documentation (a11y-43). Playwright WebKit on Windows does not reproduce iOS scrolling.

question: Do the §7.17 relative costs hold on real phones with GPU compositing, i.e. Chrome Android on a mid-range device and iOS Safari? Specifically, does the font-weight breath drop frames there, and does backdrop-filter plus the fixed star layers cost frames on weak GPUs?
howToTest: Chrome DevTools remote debugging on a mid-range Android phone: load the owner's live profile, or the scratch harness through a LAN server, and record the Performance panel with and without `#wrapper .custom-title{animation:none!important}`, then with backdrop-filter off. On an iPhone, use Safari Web Inspector's Timelines in the same three states.
whyItMatters: The measurements used a throttled desktop CPU and a desktop GPU in headless Chrome. They rank effects reliably but do not give device frame rates.

question: After 2026-10-28, are the time-bound rows still correct? random() should be in Chrome 156, scroll-driven animations in Firefox 159, and caniuse/Baseline data will have moved.
howToTest: Re-run support-probe.html and sec07-tools/sec07-probe.html in Chrome 156 (and in Firefox 159 if available, e.g. through the Playwright channels). Re-fetch BCD, web-features and caniuse as in support.md §1.4, then update §7.4, §7.7, §7.14 and the time-bound box.
whyItMatters: After those dates, guidance such as 'Chrome 155 rejects random()' or 'Firefox lacks scroll-driven animations' becomes wrong.

question: The verified grid-sizer rule has not yet been carried into the other sections that contradict it: 03 §5.4, §8.7 and §9; the 04 §1 table and §6 jam column; and 09 #15. This pass may only edit 07.
howToTest: No new test is needed. Copy the rule and the numbers from 07 §7.13 and gapfill07-01 to -03 in knowledge/evidence/gapfill.md into those sections. Optionally re-render a project page with `livegrid.mjs` to check whether any project-page grid is sized too; that was not tested.
whyItMatters: Until those sections change, an AI reading 03, 04 or 09 will still copy `#wrapper{--itchio_grid_gap}` or expect 1 column under 510px. Both silently fail on live pages.

question: Exact profile cap value and unit: characters (code points), UTF-8 bytes, or UTF-16 units?
howToTest: On mirokshi.itch.io (the account owner, manually), save exactly 5,120 ASCII characters, then 5,121. Then save 5,000 ASCII + 40 '→' (5,040 chars / 5,120 B), then 5,000 ASCII + 40 emoji (5,040 chars / 5,160 B / 5,080 UTF-16 units). After each save, note any lightbox text and run curl on the logged-out page to measure style#custom_css (e.g. with gapfill01-tools/blockstats.py). Restore dist/main.min.css afterwards.
whyItMatters: Every answer has to fit the profile budget. The section currently uses the conservative rule: ≤5,120 chars AND ≤5,120 UTF-8 bytes, with 30 spare.

question: What does an over-cap save do: reject with an error message (and what wording), or truncate and serve broken CSS?
howToTest: During the boundary test above, record the exact text of the 'Your changes were not saved, please try again' lightbox, if one appears. If the save appears to succeed, curl the served length and check whether the CSS ends mid-rule.
whyItMatters: Truncation would break pages silently. A rejection is safe but needs the right advice for users. 02 S4 and 09 #40 currently overclaim 'won't save'.

question: Does the project/devlog editor enforce any cap above 38,576 B?
howToTest: On a restricted or draft project of the owner's account, save 60,000 and then 100,000 ASCII characters of valid CSS. Record any error, then curl the served style#custom_css length (remember each newline is served as CRLF). Remove the test CSS afterwards.
whyItMatters: Git history proves a save of 38,576 B in Aug 2026. Anything larger, such as the 93,105-char live block, has an unknown save date.

question: Exact jam cap boundary: is '20kb' exactly 20,480 characters/bytes of host CSS?
howToTest: If the user hosts or co-hosts a jam (a draft jam is enough), save 20,480 then 20,481 ASCII characters in Misc → Custom CSS. Record errors and curl the overview's style#jam_theme. Measure the host part with gapfill01-tools/jamsplit.py.
whyItMatters: Jam hosts with big themes sit right at the cap. Live evidence only proves at least 20,410.

question: Is leading whitespace trimmed on save (it would be if itch uses Lapis limited_text/trim)?
howToTest: Save CSS that starts with two newlines and two spaces (e.g. '\n\n  #wrapper{}'), then curl the page and inspect the first bytes inside style#custom_css.
whyItMatters: This affects size accounting and the source-vs-live diff normalisation. It would also support or refute the Lapis-unit hypothesis (gapfill01-06).

question: Is </style> removed on save or only on render, and how are '<!--' and '<script' sequences inside CSS handled?
howToTest: In the same session, save CSS containing a comment with '</style>', then '<!--', then '<script'. Curl the served block each time and compare it byte for byte with what was pasted.
whyItMatters: A stray </style> can end the style element early and spill CSS into the page. The rule 'never write it' stands until this is tested.

question: What label and markup does the jam host's edit button have, and what is the logged-in owner DOM (.theme_editor_columns, sidebar)?
howToTest: Logged in as a host, open the jam overview and do a browser 'Save page as' (HTML only). Share the file with the csrf_token redacted. Grep it for edit_theme_btn, owner_tools and theme_editor_columns.
whyItMatters: The JS shows any .edit_theme_btn works and the wrappers are documented, but the visible label a host clicks has never been observed.

question: Does the #edit_theme hash open the editor on a phone-width viewport (profile, project and jam)?
howToTest: Logged in as the owner on a phone, or in a desktop browser emulating 375px, open https://<user>.itch.io/#edit_theme (and the jam URL + #edit_theme). Note whether the overlay editor appears and whether the Misc → Custom CSS field is usable.
whyItMatters: itch's CSS hides the Edit theme button at ≤980px, so the hash is the documented-in-code workaround. The code path does not depend on width, but it is untested live.

question: Does the profile Readme popup still link to the 404 <user>.itch.io/support?
howToTest: Logged in, open Edit theme → Misc → Readme on the profile and check the href of the 'contact us' link.
whyItMatters: A minor note: it tells users where to request help and which link to ignore.

question: Is hiding or restyling .itch_footer on jam overviews allowed by itch policy?
howToTest: Not testable by saving. Ask itch support or watch for an official statement. Re-check the guide's jam layout section periodically for a footer entry.
whyItMatters: The guide's 'do not hide these links' rule names only the project .footer. The section treats .itch_footer as protected only by inference.

question: Why did Brave Shields block the owner's `https://itch-io-custom-css-custom-css.vercel.app/live.css` import on 2026-10-12, when no default filter-list rule matches it? A headless fresh-profile Brave 1.97.56 had no active filter lists (even itch's gtag loaded), so it was inconclusive.
howToTest: A person opens https://mirokshi.itch.io/ in a normal (non-headless) Brave window. First with Shields at Standard, then at Aggressive (Shields panel, 'Trackers & ads blocking'): note whether live.css is listed as blocked and copy the matching rule from brave://adblock-internals. Also record the enabled lists in brave://settings/shields/filters, including regional lists and custom filters. Repeat in a fresh Brave profile to separate default lists from user settings.
whyItMatters: Brave users are a notable share of itch's audience. If a default rule or Aggressive mode blocks vercel.app CSS imports, per-visit services lose those visitors, and the KB should name a host or path that is not blocked.

question: Which framework class-token shapes survive itch's HTML sanitizer: `custom:flex` / `custom:md:flex` (Tailwind v4), `custom-w-1/2`, `custom-w-[37px]`, `custom-mt-[-1rem]`, `custom-bg-red-500/50`? And are `md:custom-flex`, `hover:custom-text-red-500`, `-custom-mt-4` and `!custom-flex` really dropped?
howToTest: On a test account with CSS access, save a bio (Edit profile, HTML mode) containing one `TOKEN` per shape, plus a control `custom-ok`. Log out, curl the public profile and diff the class attributes of `.user_profile` against the saved list. Also check whether a class list with one bad token keeps the good ones.
whyItMatters: This decides whether Tailwind fractions, arbitrary values, opacity modifiers or v4's prefix syntax can be used in itch HTML at all. Today the KB can only recommend plain `custom-…` words.

question: How long does an unreachable or hung @import host blank the page on macOS/iOS Safari and on Linux/macOS Chrome and Firefox? The 21 s SYN timeout measured is the Windows TCP default, and WebKit was Playwright's Windows port with its own network stack.
howToTest: Run knowledge/evidence/gapfill08-tools/stallserver.py, stallpages.py, stall-chrome.mjs and stall-pw.mjs (Playwright webkit and firefox) on macOS and Linux, plus Safari on macOS via safaridriver. Use the same 10 failure modes and a 330 s cap.
whyItMatters: It sets the real worst-case blank time for most itch visitors, and so how strict the per-visit service deadline must be.

question: What does Vercel return to the browser when a function exceeds its maxDuration (status code and body), and is a 1–5 s maxDuration honoured on Hobby?
howToTest: Deploy a Hobby function with `export const config={maxDuration:2}` that sleeps 10 s. curl -i it and record the status, headers and time to response. Then @import it from a local page in Chrome and confirm the page paints after about 2 s with the sheet ignored.
whyItMatters: §10.2 recommends a short maxDuration as the fail-fast mechanism. A non-2xx answer is known to be ignored, but the actual timeout behaviour is undocumented on the page that was read.

question: Do framework utility classes (as-is Bootstrap `.visible`, `.invisible`, `.active`, `.disabled`, `.small`, `.icon-link`) affect itch's logged-in UI, such as header dropdowns that toggle `.visible`? Only logged-out profile and project pages were diffed.
howToTest: While logged in, save a copy of a profile and a project page (or use DevTools on the live pages). Add the as-is Bootstrap import through the CSSOM (`document.getElementById('custom_css').sheet.insertRule('@import url(...)',0)` does not work for imports after rules; use a new `<style>` instead), open the header dropdowns, and diff computed styles of elements carrying those classes.
whyItMatters: It completes the collision picture for as-is imports. The renamed builds can't match itch classes by construction.
